evidence.note: Systematically compares 8 prompting strategies under equal sampling budget for majority-vote test-time scaling across 6 LLMs x 6 benchmarks, finding plain Chain-of-Thought eventually dominates every more elaborate strategy as sampling time N grows -- because CoT has more easy/fewer hard questions and a flatter wrong-answer distribution -- and shows combining per-question difficulty-adaptive scaling with per-question optimal-strategy selection lifts GSM8K accuracy from 86.0% to 97.4% (Majority@10) and MATH-500 from 15.2% to 61.0%.
evidence.title: Rethinking the Role of Prompting Strategies in LLM Test-Time Scaling: A Perspective of Probability Theory
